display.purpose: Sheet title in the title block only; no hero size.

headline.purpose: Section heads, entry titles, unit prices, the total.

body.purpose: Running text and title-block values; max 72ch.

body-sm.purpose: Specs, notes, buttons, tally amounts, merge detail.

label.purpose: Title-block labels and column heads, sentence case.

figure.purpose: Ids, keys, SKUs, dates, entry numbers, the readout.

shadows.name: margin-double-rule
shadows.value: inset 1px 0 0 var(--rule-strong), inset 4px 0 0 var(--paper), inset 5px 0 0 var(--rule-strong)
shadows.purpose: Draws the pad margin double rule; a ruling device, not elevation. Rotates to the top edge when stacked (<=1080px).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing on the pad.

motion.name: ink-in
motion.purpose: Confirmed tally line: pencil colour + 0.6px blur to graphite ink.

motion.name: pencil-draw
motion.purpose: Merge bracket stroke draws itself (stroke-dashoffset 60 to 0).

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Merge note and bracket settle from red pencil to graphite.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all animation and transition durations.

components.css: .ds-tally { max-width: 380px; font-family: var(--font-letter, 'B612', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif); font-size: 0.9375rem; color: #1d2922; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-merge { display: grid; gap: 2px; margin: 0 16px 8px 24px; padding: 6px 8px; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: #8f1d16; animation: ds-note 2.4s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) infinite alternate; } .ds-merge span { color: #3f5145; } .ds-lines { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; } .ds-line { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 3.5ch 3.5ch 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 40px; padding: 0 16px 0 24px; border-bottom: 1px dashed #86a98c; } .ds-no { align-self: stretch; display: grid; place-items: center end; padding-right: 6px; border-right: 1px solid #86a98c; color: #4f6155; font-size: 0.75rem; } .ds-qty { color: #8f1d16; font-size: 0.8125rem; } .ds-amt { text-align: right; font-size: 0.8125rem; } .ds-tag { padding: 0 4px; border: 1px solid #4f7357; color: #3f5145; font-family: var(--font-figure, 'B612 Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 0.6875rem; } .ds-bracket { position: absolute; left: 8px; top: 4px; width: 8px; height: calc(100% - 8px); overflow: visible; } .ds-bracket path { fill: none; stroke: #a8241c; stroke-width: 1.6; stroke-linecap: round; vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke; } .ds-pending, .ds-pending .ds-qty { color: #4f6155; } .ds-u { text-decoration: underline dashed #7d8e81; text-underline-offset: 4px; } .ds-total { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin: 8px 16px 0 24px; padding: 8px 0; border-top: 1.5px solid #1d2922; border-bottom: 3px double #1d2922; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.125rem; } @keyframes ds-note { 0%, 70% { background: rgb(168 36 28 / 0.09); color: #8f1d16; } 100% { background: transparent; color: #1d2922; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-merge { animation: none; background: rgb(168 36 28 / 0.09); } }

narrative.overview:
Every Cartwheel surface is a sheet torn from a pale-green engineering computation pad. A fine 8px grid with a heavier line every fifth square covers the page. A ruled title block (name, owner, date, sheet n of n) runs across the top, and the content is worked in hairline-ruled tables and margins. The sheet is lettered like a drafting office: B612 for words, B612 Mono for measured data, and tabular figures everywhere so columns of numbers line up.

Two inks are on the pad and they never mix. Graphite is the system: catalog entries, readouts, ids, latencies, rules. Red pencil is the visitor: the cart they own, the quantity they chose, the field they type in, the focus ring under their hand, and the note that marks a change to their own data. A red mark fades to graphite once it becomes history. Work in progress is drawn in pencil (a pale grey with dashed underlines) and inked once the server confirms it.

The pad is flat and dense, but it is not cramped. Nothing floats, nothing is rounded beyond 2px, and depth comes only from ruling. Columns that run out of content keep their ruled lines down to the sheet edge, the way an unused part of a pad still carries its rules.
keyCharacteristics: Pale green gridded paper with a ruled title block, not cards on a white or dark canvas.
Two inks: graphite for system data, red pencil for visitor-owned state and actions.
B612 lettering and B612 Mono figures, always with tabular numerals.
Hairline and 1.5px rules, square corners (2px at most), no elevation.
Every entry, line, and request carries a sequence number.
Pending work is pencilled, then inked. Motion draws, inks, and settles. It never bounces.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Graphite is the system and red pencil is the visitor. Red marks only state the visitor owns or just caused: their cart, their quantities, their id, their focus, a change to their data, and the failure of their own request. System data is never red, and visitor state is never graphite while it is still news.

rules.name: The Settle Rule
rules.body: Red is news, not alarm. A red note about a past event pencils in, holds, and settles to graphite (the merge note and bracket do this over 2.4s). Only red that describes the visitor's current state stays red.

rules.name: The Pencil-Then-Ink Rule
rules.body: An optimistic, unconfirmed value is drawn in Graphite Third with a dashed Pencil underline and an honest label ("pencilled", "retry 2/3"). It becomes Graphite Ink only when the server confirms it.

rules.name: The Measured-in-Mono Rule
rules.body: Machine-issued or measured values (ids, keys, SKUs, dates, calls) are set in B612 Mono with slashed zero. Money and counts stay in B612 with tabular lining figures, so decimal points stay narrow and columns still align.

rules.name: The Tabular Everywhere Rule
rules.body: The body sets tabular numerals globally. Any new number, such as a countdown, QPS, p99, or vector-clock counter, inherits it. Never switch to proportional figures for numbers that update live.

rules.name: The Ruled Continuation Rule
rules.body: A column that ends before the sheet does is not left as an empty box. The leftover space fills with ruled lines at the 40px pitch in Rule, at 55% opacity, down to the frame.

rules.name: The Numbering Rule
rules.body: Nothing is unnumbered. Catalog entries carry two-digit mono numbers (01 to 06) in their own column. Tally lines are numbered in a ruled gutter cell, so a line number never runs into a quantity. Requests carry a monotonic sequence ("#5 GET ...") in the readout, instructions are ordered lists with mono markers, and the title block states "Sheet n of n". A new list, row type, or event stream must carry its own sequence.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Raised Rule
rules.body: Separation is drawn with rules, never cast with shadows. Inset box-shadow is permitted only to draw lines, as in the margin rule.

rules.name: The Accountant's Total Rule
rules.body: A total sits under a 1.5px graphite rule and over a 3px double graphite rule.

dos: **Do** keep the two inks apart. Graphite (ink, ink-2, ink-3) for system data, red pencil (red, red-ink) only for what the visitor owns or just caused.
**Do** number every entry, line, and request, and give line numbers their own ruled gutter.
**Do** draw pending state in Graphite Third with a dashed Pencil underline and an honest label, then ink it on confirmation.
**Do** let red notes about past events settle to graphite over about 2.4s on the pad ease (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)).
**Do** continue the ruled lines (40px pitch, 55% opacity) under columns that end early.
**Do** set ids, keys, SKUs, and dates in B612 Mono with slashed zero, and keep tabular figures on every number.
**Do** honour reduced motion. The global rule collapses all animations and transitions.
donts: **Don't** cast drop shadows or raise surfaces. Inset box-shadow is for drawing rules only.
**Don't** round corners beyond 2px, and don't round frames, rows, or notes at all.
**Don't** set readable text in Pencil Grey (pencil). It is 2.9:1 and decorative only.
**Don't** use red for system data or as a general alarm colour.
**Don't** fill or shade plates. Line art is one stroke weight with a dimension line.
**Don't** imitate Amazon in colour, type, layout signatures, or terminology.
